thought.text: The `execution` is in the form action URL. Let me redo the login test correctly:

reasoning_content: The execution parameter is in the form's ACTION URL, not in a hidden input. POST to the action URL with username/password. The earlier POST to "login-actions/authenticate?client_id=local-client" (without execution) returned a 302 to authenticate with execution — that's Keycloak's redirect. A cleaner approach: extract the form's action, POST username/password there, and expect a 302 to the redirect_uri with ?code= attached.

action.command:
cat > /tmp/kc_test2.sh <<'SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
cd /workspace
eval $(grep -E "^(LOCAL_USER_EMAIL|LOCAL_USER_PASSWORD)=" .env | sed 's/^/export /')
JAR=/tmp/kc2-cookies.txt
OUT=/tmp/kc2_test.out
: > $OUT
rm -f "$JAR"
# Step 1: auth page (sets session cookies)
code=$(curl -sS -c $JAR -o /tmp/kc2-login.html -w "%{http_code}" "http://localhost:9090/realms/local/protocol/openid-connect/auth?client_id=local-client&redirect_uri=http://localhost:3000/oauth2/callback&response_type=code&scope=openid&state=teststate2" 2>>$OUT)
echo "auth-page=$code" >> $OUT
# Step 2: extract form action
ACTION=$(grep -oE '<form id="kc-form-login"[^>]*action="[^"]*"' /tmp/kc2-login.html | sed 's/.*action="//;s/"$//;s/&/\&/g')
echo "action-len=${#ACTION}" >> $OUT
# Step 3: POST credentials
res=$(curl -sS -b $JAR -c $JAR -o /tmp/kc2-login2.html -w "%{http_code}|%{redirect_url}" -X POST "$ACTION" \
  --data-urlencode "username=$LOCAL_USER_EMAIL" \
  --data-urlencode "password=$LOCAL_USER_PASSWORD" \
  --data-urlencode "signup=false" 2>>$OUT)
echo "login-post=$res" >> $OUT
# If error page, capture
grep -oE 'Invalid user or password|error=[a-z-]+' /tmp/kc2-login2.html 2>/dev/null | head -2 >> $OUT
echo "=== RESULT ==="
cat $OUT
SCRIPT
bash /tmp/kc_test2.sh
